title: Grade 10 Social Science — Nationalism in Europe & Nationalism in India
description: Nationalism in Europe and Nationalism in India practice questions
subject: social-science

questions.question: The concept of 'nation-state' was a key idea promoted by:
questions.explanation: The French Revolution of 1789 promoted the idea that sovereignty belongs to the people, not the king — a key idea behind the nation-state concept.

questions.question: The unification of Italy was largely achieved through the efforts of:
questions.explanation: Italian unification (Risorgimento) was driven by Giuseppe Mazzini (ideological inspiration), Count Cavour (political strategy), and Giuseppe Garibaldi (military campaigns). Italy unified in 1861.

questions.question: The German empire was proclaimed in:
questions.explanation: The German Empire was proclaimed in January 1871 at Versailles after Prussia's victory in the Franco-Prussian War. Otto von Bismarck unified the German states.

questions.question: The 1848 revolutions in Europe were called the 'Spring of Nations' because:
options: Multiple European nations rose in revolution demanding independence and constitutions
They resulted in new nations being formed
They were inspired by Russian spring
questions.explanation: In 1848, revolutions erupted across France, Austria, Germany, and Italy simultaneously. People demanded constitutional rights, national independence, and liberal reforms — hence called the Spring of Nations.

questions.question: The Congress of Vienna (1815) was convened to:
options: Restore conservative monarchies and pre-Napoleon order in Europe
questions.explanation: The Congress of Vienna (1815) was hosted by Prince Metternich to restore the conservative order and redraw Europe's map after Napoleon's defeat, suppressing liberal and nationalist movements.

questions.question: Which artist's painting 'Germania' symbolised German nationalism?
questions.explanation: Philip Veit's 'Germania' depicted a female allegory of the German nation as a symbol of German national unity and pride — a common Romantic nationalist imagery.

questions.question: Zollverein (1834) was a:
options: Customs union that removed trade barriers between German states
questions.explanation: Zollverein was a customs union of German states initiated by Prussia in 1834 that abolished tariffs between member states. It created economic unity that preceded political unification.

questions.question: The Balkan region was called 'the powder keg of Europe' because:
options: Competing nationalisms and great power rivalries created extreme political tension
questions.explanation: The Balkans were fragmented with Slavic nationalism, Ottoman decline, and rival interests of Austria-Hungary and Russia. This explosive combination ultimately triggered World War I in 1914.

questions.question: The Non-Cooperation Movement was launched by Mahatma Gandhi in:
questions.explanation: The Non-Cooperation Movement was launched in 1920 in response to the Rowlatt Act (1919) and the Jallianwala Bagh massacre. It called for boycott of British goods, institutions, and titles.

questions.question: The Dandi March (Salt March) was undertaken in:
questions.explanation: Gandhi led the Salt March from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi (Gujarat) in March-April 1930 to protest the British salt tax. This began the Civil Disobedience Movement.

questions.question: The Rowlatt Act (1919) was opposed because:
options: It allowed detention without trial and repressed civil liberties
questions.explanation: The Rowlatt Act allowed the British to imprison anyone suspected of revolutionary activity without trial. Gandhi called it 'Black Act' and organized peaceful hartals (strikes) against it.

questions.question: The Quit India Movement was launched in:
questions.explanation: Gandhi launched the Quit India Movement ('Do or Die') in August 1942, demanding immediate British withdrawal from India. The slogan was 'Karenge ya marenge' — Do or Die.

questions.question: The partition of Bengal (1905) was undertaken by:
questions.explanation: Lord Curzon partitioned Bengal in 1905 into Hindu-majority West Bengal and Muslim-majority East Bengal. It was opposed by Indian nationalists who saw it as a divide-and-rule strategy.

questions.question: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre occurred on:
questions.explanation: On 13 April 1919 (Baisakhi Day), General Dyer ordered troops to fire on a peaceful unarmed gathering at Jallianwala Bagh, Amritsar, killing hundreds. This shocked the nation.

questions.question: The Indian National Congress was founded in:
questions.explanation: The Indian National Congress (INC) was founded in 1885 by A.O. Hume, with Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee as its first president, in Bombay.
